newsitem.title: INDIA: Rebel leader killed in Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: Rebel leader killed in Kashmir.

text.p: A leader of the hardline Hizb-ul-Mujahideen militant group fighting Indian rule in Kashmir has been killed, police and separatists said on Friday.
Police said Mohammad Yousuf Ganie, deputy chief commander of Hizb-ul-Mujahideen, was killed in a gunbattle with police on Thursday evening.
The battle occurred near Anantnag town, 60 km (35 miles) south of the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir state, Srinagar, they said.

Hizb-ul-Mujahideen, one of more than a dozen militant separatist groups operating in the Himalayan region, said in a written statement distributed to news organisations in Srinagar that Ganie was tortured to death by Indian security forces.
Hizb-ul-Mujahideen is fighting for merger of the Himalayan state with neighbouring Pakistan.
Police and hospital officials say more than 20,000 people have been killed in a seven-year-old separatist rebellion in mostly Hindu India'ts only Moslem majority state.
Two of the three wars fought between India and Pakistan since they gained independence in 1947 have been triggered by disputes over Jammu and Kashmir state.
